items.author: Nell Garside
items.title: Revealed: the Bristol roads with the most collisions
items.body: A Western Ledger analysis of Department for Transport collision records for 2021 to 2025 has identified the Bristol roads where people are most often hurt in crashes. Wellsford Road in Fishponds tops the list with 41 recorded injury collisions over five years, ahead of Kingsmere Road (34), Alder Hill (31), Tanner's Way (29) and Crossfield Road (27). The analysis covers roads within the city council boundary and counts collisions in which at least one person was injured. [CORRECTION, 6 November 2026: An earlier version of this article overstated the number of collisions on Wellsford Road. The correct figure is 23, which places it sixth. The table has been updated. A full explanation will follow on the Data Desk blog.]

items.author: martin.okoro@westernledger.example
items.title: Wellsford Road - explainer for the blog
items.body: Nell, correction's live. Thanks for turning it round quickly. For the Data Desk explainer, standards need it to cover: what went wrong in plain terms, the corrected figures, what we are changing in our process, and an apology to residents for the impact. It goes under your byline. Apart from your own byline, please do not name any individual, inside or outside the building, and do not get into the rights and wrongs of the council's 20mph proposals; that is not our fight. Send me the draft before anything is scheduled. Martin

items.author: deborah.lyle@fishpondsstreets.example
items.title: Your 'most dangerous road' story
items.body: Ms Garside, I chair the Fishponds Streets Forum. Your article of 2 November has been shared hundreds of times and Wellsford Road is now being described locally as 'the deadliest road in Bristol'. Several of us have lived on it for decades and simply did not recognise the figure. One of our members went through the published DfT data herself and could not get anywhere near 41. Parents have been asking whether it is safe to walk children to Wellsford Primary. If you have made an error, we expect it to be acknowledged as prominently as the original claim, and we expect to understand how it happened. Deborah Lyle, Chair, Fishponds Streets Forum

items.author: Nell Garside
items.title: Wellsford recheck - working notes
items.body: Cause: The join duplicated some collision–road pairs, so the same accident index appeared twice within a road’s tally. Eighteen duplicate entries were removed from Wellsford Road’s total, mostly at Pell Street and Kingsmere Road junctions. We now count each accident index once per road. Wellsford Road: 41 -> 23. Kingsmere Road: 34 -> 32. Alder Hill: 31 -> 31. Tanner's Way: 29 -> 28. Crossfield Road: 27 -> 26. New fifth: Hambrook Lane, 24. Wellsford now 6th. Of Wellsford's 23, three serious, none fatal. Whole citywide table rerun, no other road moves more than two places. Fix: second analyst reproduces any ranked table before publication; publish the cleaned dataset and code alongside.

items.author: Fishponds Streets Forum (Facebook group)
items.title: Ledger 'correction'
items.body: So the Ledger has quietly changed 41 to 23 and stuck a line at the bottom of the article. That's nearly half. The headline still says 'Revealed'. Comments: 'Who checks this stuff?' / 'My neighbour had a buyer pull out on Thursday, coincidence?' / 'To be fair they did correct it within days, more than most' / 'Still 23 crashes, the road isn't perfect either' / 'I want to know HOW you get 18 crashes out of nowhere.'

items.author: cllr.faisal.rahman@bristolcouncillors.example
items.title: Wellsford figure
items.body: Nell, I quoted your 41 figure in our ward newsletter supporting the 20mph consultation. I gather it's been revised. Can you confirm the corrected number so I can put out an update? I'd rather not be accused of scaremongering. Thanks, Faisal

items.author: Joss Whitlock
items.body: between us, Callum ran that join in his last week before he left for the Post and nobody second-checked it because we were short. not your fault really. but don't put that anywhere obviously

items.author: legal@westernledger.example
items.title: PRIVILEGED: letter from Hollis Pryce LLP
items.body: We have received a letter from Hollis Pryce LLP acting for Avonmere Lettings alleging loss of business on Wellsford Road following the article. We do not consider it has merit, but please make no public reference to the letter, the firm or their client in any published material, including the forthcoming explainer. Legal
